title_en: Huang Weizhong v. Chen Qiangqing et al. — dispute over confirmation of shareholder qualification
ruling_gist_en: Without a valid shareholders' resolution of the company, if a third party makes a false capital increase to the company in order to 'dilute' the shares of the original shareholders, such act infringes upon the legitimate rights and interests of the original shareholders. Even if such capital contribution has been registered with the administrative authority for industry and commerce, it shall still be deemed invalid, and the original shareholders' equity proportions shall remain unchanged.

full_text_en:
Huang Weizhong v. Chen Qiangqing et al. — dispute over confirmation of shareholder qualification

Ruling Summary

Where a third party falsely makes a capital contribution to a company to "dilute" the shares of the company's existing shareholders without a valid resolution of the shareholders' meeting, such conduct impairs the legitimate rights and interests of the existing shareholders. Even if the capital contribution has been recorded and filed with the administrative authority for industry and commerce, it shall still be deemed invalid, and the equity proportions of the company's original shareholders shall remain unchanged.

Plaintiff: Huang Weizhong, male, 43 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Baoshan District, Shanghai.

Defendant: Chen Qiangqing, male, 56 years old, Han Chinese, residing at Wenshui East Road, Shanghai.

Defendant: Chen Lin, male, 60 years old, Han Chinese, residing at Shuichan West Road, Shanghai.

Defendant: Zhang Yang, male, 56 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Baoshan District, Shanghai.

Defendant: Gu Huiping, male, 54 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Baoshan District, Shanghai.

Defendant: Shanghai Xinbao Construction and Installation Engineering Co., Ltd., domiciled at Baoshan District, Shanghai.

Legal representative: Zhang Yang, Chairman of the Board of the company.

Defendant: Wang Xiuying, female, 57 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Baoshan District, Shanghai.

Defendant: Jiangsu Ennas Heavy Industry Machinery Co., Ltd., domiciled at Minying Industrial Zone, Fuqiao Town, Taicang City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal representative: Wang Leiming, Chairman of the Board of the company.

The plaintiff, Huang Weizhong, filed an action with the Hongkou District People's Court of Shanghai against the defendants Chen Qiangqing, Chen Lin, Zhang Yang, Gu Huiping, Shanghai Xinbao Construction and Installation Engineering Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xinbao Company), Wang Xiuying, and Jiangsu Ennas Heavy Industry Machinery Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jiangsu Ennas Company) concerning a dispute over shareholder qualification.

Plaintiff's Allegations: In April 2004, Huang Weizhong and defendant Chen Qiangqing, among others, jointly established Taicang Hongguan Steel Structure Products Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hongguan Company) with a registered capital of RMB 4 million, of which Huang Weizhong contributed RMB 800,000, holding 20% of the shares. Thereafter, all shareholders of Hongguan Company entrusted Chen Qiangqing to handle the transfer of the company's equity. The transferee, Jiangsu Ennas Company, was to transfer the corresponding equity transfer price to Chen Qiangqing's personal account; however, Chen Qiangqing delayed in paying the corresponding amount to the plaintiff. Accordingly, the plaintiff filed a lawsuit on the ground of a dispute over an entrustment contract. During the litigation, Chen Qiangqing and others informed the plaintiff for the first time of the company's capital increase and the adjustment of equity proportions, and the plaintiff's equity proportion had been adjusted to 5.33%. On May 24, 2011, upon inquiry into the industrial and commercial registration records of Hongguan Company, the plaintiff discovered the alleged capital increase. However, the plaintiff had no knowledge whatsoever of the alleged capital increase prior to that time and had never signed any shareholders' meeting resolution concerning such capital increase. Moreover, the RMB 11 million that Xinbao Company allegedly invested in Hongguan Company was transferred out immediately after the capital verification, and the company never actually effected any capital increase. In addition, when the transferee acquired the equity of Hongguan Company, the transfer price did not take into account all the increased capital. Therefore, the capital increase of Hongguan Company was fictitious and invalid. Accordingly, the plaintiff prayed for a judgment confirming that Huang Weizhong held 20% of the equity in Hongguan Company during the period from the establishment of Hongguan Company on April 1, 2004 to the equity transfer on June 6, 2009 (the specific period of shareholding to be determined by the court based on relevant evidentiary materials).

Defendants Chen Qiangqing, Chen Lin, Zhang Yang, and Gu Huiping argued: After the establishment of Hongguan Company, pursuant to the policies and regulations of the local government, if a company engages in land development business, its registered capital must reach RMB 15 million. Therefore, in September 2006, Hongguan Company, by a resolution of the shareholders' meeting, resolved to admit Xinbao Company as a shareholder for the purpose of a capital increase, and the plaintiff was aware of this. Even if the plaintiff was not aware of the shareholders' meeting resolution, he should have become aware of the capital increase when the equity of Hongguan Company was transferred to Jiangsu Ennas Company in June 2009. Thus, the plaintiff's claim is time-barred. As for the RMB 11 million capital increase, although the amount was transferred back to Xinbao Company after the capital increase of Hongguan Company, the nature of the sum changed and became a loan from Xinbao Company to Hongguan Company.

Defendant Xinbao Company argued: At the time of the establishment of Hongguan Company, the plaintiff had not actually made a capital contribution but had borrowed RMB 800,000 from Xinbao Company. Xinbao Company specially convened a shareholders' meeting of Xinbao Company for the purpose of investing in Hongguan Company, and the plaintiff, who was then a shareholder of Xinbao Company, also signed the resolution.

Defendant Wang Xiuying argued: She agreed with the plaintiff's opinion. After the establishment of Hongguan Company, she had always held 10% of the company's equity, and the company's equity structure had never changed subsequently. She had never been informed of the company's capital increase, nor had she participated in any shareholders' meeting concerning the capital increase, and had never signed the alleged shareholders' meeting resolution.

Defendant Jiangsu Ennas Company argued: As the transferee of the equity, the transferee had fully paid the equity transfer price in accordance with the requirements of the transfer contract and the equity transfer confirmation letter.

The court of first instance, the Hongkou District People's Court of Shanghai, found the following facts:

On April 21, 2004, the plaintiff Huang Weizhong together with the defendants Chen Qiangqing, Chen Lin, Zhang Yang, Gu Huiping, and Wang Xiuying jointly established Hongguan Company with a registered capital of RMB 4 million, of which: Zhang Yang contributed RMB 1.2 million, holding 30%; Huang Weizhong and Gu Huiping each contributed RMB 800,000, each holding 20%; Chen Lin, Chen Qiangqing, and Wang Xiuying each contributed RMB 400,000, each holding 10%.

On October 20, 2006, upon the application of Hongguan Company, the Taicang Administration for Industry and Commerce, Suzhou, changed the registered capital of Hongguan Company from RMB 4 million to RMB 15 million, and at the same time changed the registration of shareholders and shareholding proportions to: Zhang Yang contributed RMB 1.2 million, holding 8.00%; Huang Weizhong and Gu Huiping each contributed RMB 800,000, each holding 5.33%; Chen Lin, Chen Qiangqing, and Wang Xiuying each contributed RMB 400,000, each holding 2.67%; Xinbao Company contributed RMB 11 million, holding 73.33%. The main bases for applying for the above registration changes were the "Articles of Association of Taicang Hongguan Steel Structure Products Co., Ltd." and the "Resolution of the Shareholders' Meeting of Taicang Hongguan Steel Structure Products Co., Ltd.," both dated October 16, 2006. The main change in the content of the articles of association was: the registered capital of Hongguan Company was increased from the original RMB 4 million to RMB 15 million; Xinbao Company was added as a shareholder, etc. The main content recorded in the shareholders' meeting resolution was: approval of the amended articles of association; increase of the company's registered capital from the original RMB 4 million to RMB 15 million, with Xinbao Company increasing its investment by RMB 11 million, etc.

During the first instance trial, the defendant Xinbao Company and others produced a "Resolution of the Shareholders' General Meeting of Shanghai Xinbao Construction and Installation Engineering Co., Ltd." dated September 26, 2006 and the "Articles of Association of Taicang Hongguan Steel Structure Products Co., Ltd." dated September 28, 2006, which respectively stated: "On September 26, 2006, a general meeting of all shareholders was convened in the meeting room of Shanghai Xinbao Construction and Installation Engineering Co., Ltd. All shareholders discussed and agreed to invest RMB 11 million in cash in Taicang Hongguan Steel Structure Products Co., Ltd." and "On September 28, 2006, a meeting of all shareholders was convened in the meeting room of the preparatory office of Taicang Hongguan Steel Structure Products Co., Ltd. All shareholders expressed their agreement to Shanghai Xinbao Construction and Installation Engineering Co., Ltd. investing in the company."

On May 21, 2009, the defendant Chen Qiangqing, as the shareholder representative of Hongguan Company, entered into an equity transfer contract with Suzhou Ennas Company, whereby Suzhou Ennas Company purchased all the equity of Hongguan Company at a price of RMB 8,248,500. The transferee, Suzhou Ennas Company, was tentatively designated as one company, and the final list of shareholders was to be provided before the formal handling of the equity transfer. On June 24, 2009, the Taicang Administration for Industry and Commerce, Suzhou, issued a "Notice of Approval of Company Change Registration," stating that the original shareholders of Jiangsu Ennas Company had been changed from the plaintiff Huang Weizhong, the defendants Chen Qiangqing, Chen Lin, Zhang Yang, Gu Huiping, Wang Xiuying, and Xinbao Company to Suzhou Ennas Company and Nantong Yuanhua Trading Co., Ltd., and that the above change had been filed with the industrial and commercial authority, etc.

During the trial, as the plaintiff Huang Weizhong and the defendant Wang Xiuying both denied the authenticity of the above articles of association and shareholders' meeting resolution, the defendant Xinbao Company filed an application requesting a handwriting comparison to determine whether the handwriting of "Huang Weizhong" on the shareholders' general meeting resolution of Xinbao Company dated September 26, 2006 and the shareholders' meeting resolution of Hongguan Company dated September 28, 2006 was that of Huang Weizhong. The expert opinion concluded that the signatures of "Huang Weizhong" on the two resolutions were not written by the same person who wrote the comparison sample signatures of "Huang Weizhong."

It was further found that, according to the articles of association of Hongguan Company, an increase in the company's registered capital should be resolved by the company's shareholders' meeting and be passed by shareholders representing more than two-thirds of the voting rights. The RMB 11 million that the defendant Xinbao Company used for the alleged capital increase of Hongguan Company was, after the completion of capital verification on October 18, 2006, returned to Xinbao Company in the form of a "loan."

The issue in dispute at first instance was: whether Hongguan Company had effected a lawful and valid capital increase and its impact on the plaintiff Huang Weizhong's shareholding proportion.

The Hongkou District People's Court of Shanghai held at first instance: In the absence of the plaintiff Huang Weizhong disposing of his equity in accordance with the company's articles of association, unless Hongguan Company had carried out a lawful capital increase, the plaintiff's shareholding proportion should not be reduced. The defendants Xinbao Company and others argued that Hongguan Company had completed a capital increase of RMB 11 million on October 20, 2006 and provided the so-called shareholders' meeting resolution in support thereof. However, given that the plaintiff and the defendant Wang Xiuying denied this, the defendants Xinbao Company and others failed to provide sufficient evidence to prove the authenticity of these written documents. On the contrary, the handwriting comparison opinion concerning "Huang Weizhong" further confirmed the fact that Huang Weizhong had not signed the relevant shareholders' meeting resolution. It could thus be inferred that Huang Weizhong, Chen Qiangqing, Chen Lin, Zhang Yang, Gu Huiping, and Wang Xiuying, as the former shareholders of Hongguan Company, had not convened a shareholders' meeting concerning the capital increase of RMB 11 million for Hongguan Company. In the absence of a convened shareholders' meeting, the so-called capital increase of RMB 11 million for Hongguan Company violated the company's articles of association and the law and was invalid. Furthermore, as a matter of consequence, the RMB 11 million used by Hongguan Company for the so-called capital increase was, after the completion of capital verification, returned to Xinbao Company in the form of a "loan." Under such circumstances, it could not be deemed that Xinbao Company had fulfilled its capital contribution obligation. Therefore, the court determined that Hongguan Company had not actually completed a capital increase on October 20, 2006, and that the reduction of the plaintiff's shareholding proportion in the name of a capital increase infringed upon the plaintiff's legitimate rights and interests.

In conclusion, the Hongkou District People's Court of Shanghai, pursuant to Article 38, paragraph 1, item 7 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 64, paragraph 1 and Article 130 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 2 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, rendered the following judgment on December 31, 2012:

It is confirmed that the plaintiff Huang Weizhong held 20% of the equity in Taicang Hongguan Steel Structure Products Co., Ltd. (whose name has been changed to Jiangsu Ennas Heavy Industry Machinery Co., Ltd.) during the period from April 21, 2004 to June 24, 2009.

Xinbao Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court. The appellant argued that Huang Weizhong knew that he had not made a capital contribution but had instead borrowed funds from Xinbao Company to jointly register and establish Hongguan Company with others. At that time, Huang Weizhong was a shareholder of Xinbao Company and served as its manager. After the registration of Hongguan Company was completed, the registered capital was returned to Xinbao Company, and Hongguan Company did not actually operate. With the financing from the registered shareholders and persons not party to the case, they planned to purchase land in the industrial park. Due to local policy restrictions, Hongguan Company needed to increase its capital before it could make the purchase. Huang Weizhong stated that he also contributed funds to purchase the land, which clearly indicated that he was aware of the need for a capital increase. Huang Weizhong had entrusted others with full authority to handle the equity transfer process. It is clearly inconsistent with common sense for him now to deny his knowledge by claiming that he did not sign the relevant capital increase documents.

Upon second instance trial, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court confirmed the facts found by the court of first instance.

The Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court held at second instance: Hongguan Company was jointly established with capital contributions by the appellee Huang Weizhong and the defendants at first instance Chen Qiangqing, Chen Lin, Zhang Yang, Gu Huiping, and Wang Xiuying. At the time of establishment, the plaintiff lawfully held 20% of the equity in Hongguan Company. In the absence of Huang Weizhong disposing of his equity, unless Hongguan Company had carried out a lawful capital increase, the plaintiff's shareholding proportion should not be reduced. The articles of association of Hongguan Company explicitly provided that an increase in the company's capital should be resolved by the shareholders' meeting. Following the handwriting comparison, it was established that the signatures on the shareholders' meeting resolutions of Hongguan Company and Xinbao Company were not those of Huang Weizhong himself. Therefore, it could not be determined from the written shareholders' meeting resolutions that Huang Weizhong knew of the capital increase. There was no necessary causal connection between contributing funds to purchase land and a company capital increase. Accordingly, in the absence of evidence proving that Huang Weizhong knew of and signed the shareholders' meeting resolution consenting to the increase of Hongguan Company's capital to RMB 15 million, the capital increase was invalid as among the internal shareholders existing at the time of Hongguan Company's establishment, and it had no binding legal effect on Huang Weizhong. The registered capital amount of RMB 15 million as recorded in the industrial and commercial change registration should not be used to reduce Huang Weizhong's shareholding proportion in Hongguan Company; instead, equity distribution among the shareholders internally should still be based on the 20% equity proportion. The court of first instance correctly applied the law, the trial procedure was lawful, and there was no error in its judgment that Huang Weizhong held 20% of the equity in Hongguan Company from the time of its establishment until the equity transfer.

In conclusion, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Article 170, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on April 11, 2013:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

This judgment is final.
